note: Standout experiments, kept by hand from the publisher's own page and press coverage. Add new entries here. Every field must come from the source.

items.title: Claude Fable 5 plays Pokémon FireRed using only screenshots
items.summary: Anthropic's Fable 5 launch announcement shows Claude finishing Pokémon FireRed from game screenshots alone.
items.what: In the Fable 5 launch announcement, Anthropic says Claude Fable 5 beat Pokémon FireRed with a minimal, vision-only harness.
items.setup: It received only raw game screenshots, with no game-state data. Press coverage says earlier models struggled even with helper harnesses.
items.result: It completed the game with vision alone. Anthropic's announcement also carries a time-lapse video of the run.

items.title: Project Vend: Claude runs a small shop in an experiment
items.summary: Anthropic and Andon Labs let a Claude instance, nicknamed Claudius, run an automated shop in Anthropic's San Francisco office for about a month.
items.what: A Claude Sonnet 3.7 agent, Claudius, ran a small office shop for about a month, in a test with Andon Labs.
items.setup: Told to make a profit, it could search the web, email wholesalers, keep notes, chat with staff on Slack and change prices. Andon Labs staff did the physical restocking.
items.result: The shop did not make money. Claudius sold items below cost, gave discounts when pressed and once took payment through a made-up Venmo account, but it also found niche suppliers and launched a pre-order service.

items.title: Project Vend phase two: an experiment adding a CEO agent to the shop
items.summary: The second phase of Anthropic's AI shop experiment added a CEO agent and a merch agent and grew the business to three cities.
items.what: Phase two moved the shopkeeper to newer Claude models, added a CEO agent (Seymour Cash) and a merch-making agent (Clothius), and grew from one San Francisco machine to San Francisco, New York and London.
items.setup: New tools: a customer system, better inventory data, web research for suppliers, payment links and reminders. Purchases still needed human approval.
items.result: Weeks with negative margins were largely eliminated and the merch sold well. The CEO cut discounts by about 80%, but the shop was still easy to manipulate, for example with a fake contract.

items.title: Project Deal: Claude agents negotiate secondhand sales in an experiment
items.summary: For one week, Claude agents bought, sold and negotiated used items for 69 Anthropic employees in Slack.
items.what: 69 Anthropic employees each gave an agent a $100 budget to buy and sell secondhand items, negotiating in Slack with no human sign-off.
items.setup: Four parallel markets ran. In the real one every agent was Claude Opus 4.5; in two others each person was randomly given Opus 4.5 or the smaller Haiku 4.5.
items.result: The real market made 186 deals worth just over $4,000. Opus agents closed about 2.1 more deals per person than Haiku agents, but people rated both about the same on fairness.

items.title: Project Swap: Claude agents trade books for 201 people in an experiment
items.summary: Anthropic's Economics team had Claude agents swap books on behalf of 201 employees across six offices to see what works when agents trade for people.
items.what: 201 employees each brought a book; Claude learned their taste in a short chat, then their agents proposed and accepted swaps on an open trading floor.
items.setup: The team reran the floors dozens of times with different Claude models and with 'ruthless' or 'prosocial' instructions.
items.result: Claude matched people's own book rankings on 61% of pairs (50% is chance). All-Opus floors scored 0.88 on a 0 to 1 satisfaction scale against 0.75 for all-Haiku; the instructions mattered little.
